correctness.rationale: The Zak sum factors on tensor products, giving exactly the stated windows and support. On a fundamental strip B=psi(u)>0; A is positive real for 0<u<1/2, vanishes at 1/2, and on 1/2<u<1 the ratio is R(u)exp(2 pi i v). Both differences in L'=d log R/du are positive there, and R has endpoints 0 and infinity, yielding precisely one positive-Jacobian preimage for each slit-plane root. At an integer u, B=0 but A is nonzero, so no factor of the coefficient polynomial can be identically zero and the simultaneous coefficient equations exclude such a pole. Off the poles, equality of monic polynomials forces exactly the d! permutations. The absolute complex determinant of the coefficient map is the absolute Vandermonde (evaluate coefficient variations at the simple roots); its real determinant is the square of that modulus. The product prefactor contributes |prod B_j|^(2d), and each ratio contributes 2 pi |rho_j|^2 L'(u_j). This is the displayed permutation-invariant positive determinant in paired orientation. The sign convention for c1 can also be checked directly by the single positive transverse zero in d=1; the general Zak line is the tensor product of the pullbacks of those coordinate lines. Therefore the Euler number of its d-fold direct sum is d!, giving the stated lower bound exactly in the transverse case. The frozen Python checker is finite floating-point corroboration for d=1 through 5, not a global zero search; it was inspected, not executed. The decision rests on the exact analytic reconstruction.
